plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Ultraviolet Inactivation & PrP Conformational Conversion chart from Alper, Cramp, Haig & Clarke (20 May 1967 Nature 214: 764–766), Griffith (9 September 1967 Nature 215: 1043–1044), Prusiner (9 April 1982 Science 216: 136–144), Pan et al. (2 July 1993 Cell 73: 1339–1347) plots log survival against 254 nm UV dose and compares normal PrPC (43% alpha-helix, 3% beta-sheet, protease-sensitive) against infectious PrPSc (30% alpha-helix, 43% beta-sheet, protease-resistant).

teach_overlay.label: 1967 ALPER 254 NM UV SURVIVAL CURVE & 1982/1993 PRUSINER PRPC (43% α-HELIX, 3% β-SHEET) → PRPSC (43% β-SHEET) CONVERSION
teach_overlay.detail: Inked UV radiation survival & PrPC-to-PrPSc secondary-structure chart on period paper contrasting nucleic-acid viruses (inactivated by 254 nm UV light) with the scrapie prion agent (resistant to 254 nm UV, nucleases, and 100 °C boiling, inactivated by protein-denaturing proteases/chaotropes) as normal PrPC (43% alpha-helix, 3% beta-sheet) refolds into PrPSc (43% beta-sheet)
teach_overlay.scale: a prion is not a living parasite with its own genetic blueprint — it is a single misfolded crystal seed that snaps normal springy brain proteins into flat rigid sheets on contact, like one toppling domino knocking down an entire room
